pr_title: drivers: udc_stm32: Implement driver API to get actual device speed and fix ZLP handling
pr_body:
Implement driver API to get actual device speed and handle ZLP flag.
Both of these fixes are required for the driver to work properly.

Fixes https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/issues/68817

issue_context.title: usb: udp: frames of exact multiples of 64 Byte not transmitted correctly
comments:
Hi @Aluleichtbau! We appreciate you submitting your first issue for our open-source project. 🌟

Even though I'm a bot, I can assure you that the whole community is genuinely grateful for your time and effort. 🤖💙

@jfischer-no 
This bug breaks the communication in my case. I am using CoAP on top of it. Simple requests are very likely to have this problem. I have a lot of 64 byte messages. Only the first of the sequence of 64-byte messages on the wire gets an response and there are messages that never get a response because of this.

Please try an in-tree sample like `samples/net/zperf` and on the host side

```bash
#!/bin/bash

IP=$1

for (( n=0; n<1; n++ ))
do
        for (( packetsize=0; packetsize<1025; packetsize=$packetsize+1 ))
        do
                ping -i 0.002 -c 10 -s $packetsize -q $IP
        done
done
```

> Please try an in-tree sample like `samples/net/zperf` and on the host side

@jfischer-no 

I had to perform some extra steps to make zperf work with the new usb device stack (configured device descriptor).

```
ping -i 500 -c 1 -s 21 -q $IP
ping -i 500 -c 1 -s 22 -q $IP
ping -i 500 -c 1 -s 23 -q $IP
```

... resulted in this:

![2024-02-21_ping_lump](https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/assets/32814338/a28a6ac6-1ea0-4162-bd27-3f9e23e06094)

The monitoring has been done on USBcap interface.

The problem can be observed when the device replies to the ICMP request with packetsize 22, 86 (22+64), ..., (22+64*n). Some replies fail, some are successful, but all of the replies contain non-empty Ethernet trailer.

With a sample sending UDP packages with incrementing lengths the same problem is observed (also starts with 22 UDP data length, step is also 64).

> > Please try an in-tree sample like `samples/net/zperf` and on the host side
> 
> @jfischer-no
> 
> I had to perform some extra steps to make zperf work with the new usb device stack (configured device descriptor).

Shell commands can be used for this.

> With a sample sending UDP packages with incrementing lengths the same problem is observed (also starts with 22 UDP data length, step is also 64).

Looks like a bug in the new experimental STM32 shim driver, IIRC ZLP flag handling is missing. I have a patch somewhere. Will update this comment asap.
